about: Sanitized stored state written by released iTerm2 versions. See README.md.

3.4.0.vm: macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), arm64, no Rosetta; VM vm1, user account vmuser01
steps: Start from clean state in the VM: quit iTerm2, kill iTermServer and the tmux server, remove ~/Library/Preferences/com.googlecode.iterm2*.plist, ~/Library/Application Support/iTerm2, ~/Library/Saved Application State/com.googlecode.iterm2.savedState, ~/Library/Caches/com.googlecode.iterm2, ~/Library/HTTPStorages/com.googlecode.iterm2*, ~/Library/WebKit/com.googlecode.iterm2, ~/.config/iterm2, ~/corpus-prefs, ~/corpus-logs, ~/corpus-fake; killall cfprefsd; confirm `defaults read com.googlecode.iterm2` reports the domain missing.
Create ~/corpus-fake/fake-background.png (an icon converted with sips) and ~/corpus-logs.
Launch the downloaded app with `open -n ~/corpus-work/dl/<ver>/iTerm.app` (the app runs from outside /Applications, without -suite, on the real com.googlecode.iterm2 domain).

First launch: answer the Move to Applications prompt with Don't ask again + Do Not Move; close What's New; Cmd-N; type `echo PANE_A`; Cmd-Q and confirm. This makes the app write its first-launch defaults and profile.

With the app quit, run tools/configure.py from this corpus, which edits the domain through `defaults export`/`defaults import` (binary plist): profile 0 renamed Fake Default with many typed fields changed (colors with and without Color Space/Alpha, Menlo 14 + Courier 13 non-ASCII font, spacing 1.05/1.1, vertical bar cursor, blinking, badge text with interpolation, background image path, blend, transparency, blur, automatic plain-text logging to ~/corpus-logs, Logging Style, 4321 scrollback lines, custom command /bin/zsh -l, custom working directory, 100x30, option keys, bells, Unicode version 9, answerback, title components, custom window title, status bar on, tags, 4 triggers (Highlight, Alert, Bell, Mark), 2 smart selection rules, bound host fakehost.example, semantic history, two extra Keyboard Map entries); profile Fake Second (unlimited scrollback, underline cursor, Recycle directory, shortcut S, tab color); profile Fake Hotkey (hotkey window: Cmd-Opt-Ctrl-H, window type 2, floats, animates; Advanced working directory settings); GlobalKeyMap entry Cmd-Opt-Ctrl-F sending text; general/appearance/keys/pointer globals (SavePasteHistory, tab style, tab position, hide scrollbar, border, dimming, pane titles, status bar position, switch tab/window modifiers, left option); 15 advanced settings of int, float, string and bool types (MinTabWidth, OptimumTabWidth, PasteHistoryMaxOptions, XtermVersion, TabFlashAnimationDuration, TimeBetweenBlinks, BellRateLimit, BadgeFont, DefaultURLScheme, ViewManPageCommand, UseUnevenTabs, TabsWrapAround, FullHeightCursor, DisableTabBarTooltips, MiddleClickClosesTab). It also writes DynamicProfiles/fake-dynamic.json with Fake Dynamic Parent and Fake Dynamic Child (child of the dynamic parent via Dynamic Profile Parent Name).
Relaunch. Decline automatic update checks (Don't Check). Deny every macOS input-control (Device Control and Data Access) request for iTerm.
Click the status bar, drag Clock, CPU Utilization and Search into Active Components, OK (writes Status Bar Layout through the app; the app then rewrites the whole New Bookmarks array).
Profiles > Other Actions > Save All Profiles as JSON to ~/corpus-fake/fake-all-profiles.json.
Pointer: toggle Focus window after right or middle click; Bindings: add Middle Button, Double Click, Option, Send Text 'fake pointer text'.

Shortcuts > Actions: add 'Fake Next Tab Action' (Next Tab). Snippets: after replacing the VM clipboard with fake text, add 'Fake Snippet Title' / 'echo fake snippet value' (tag fake-snippet-tag where the version has tags).

Window layout: source ~/corpus-work/si.zsh (tools/si.zsh in this corpus; a fake shell integration that reports RemoteHost fakeuser@fakehost.example, CurrentDir, and OSC 133 marks) so command and directory history are recorded; run fake commands (ls, echo fake-alert-1, echo FAKE-ERROR one); set tab title 'Fake Tab One' and tab color with OSC 1 / OSC 6; Cmd-D and Cmd-Shift-D splits; Shell > Split Horizontally... with profile Fake Second, title 'Fake Second Pane Title', maximize that pane (Cmd-Shift-Return); Cmd-T second tab titled 'Fake Tab Two' with another tab color; Cmd-N second window; in it start `tmux -CC new -s fakesession` (Homebrew tmux), add a tmux split and a tmux tab; open and hide the hotkey window with Cmd-Opt-Ctrl-H. Automatic profile switching moved some sessions to Fake Dynamic Child because the fake RemoteHost matches a Bound Hosts entry.
Cmd-Shift-S: save arrangement 'Fake Complex'.
Paste two lines of fake text (on 3.5.0 and later the multi-line paste warning appears; answer Remember my choice + Paste); Cmd-F search for 'fakesearchterm'.
Cmd-Q with all windows open and confirm (restoration policy left at its default, Use System Window Restoration Setting). The <ver>-restore1 set is captured here.
Relaunch (windows restore), Cmd-N a one-tab window, close the tmux gateway window and the main window, Cmd-Shift-S: save 'Fake Simple'.
Settings > Arrangements: Set Default on Fake Simple, then on Fake Complex (Default Arrangement Name = Fake Complex).

Settings > General > Preferences/Settings: Load from custom folder ~/corpus-prefs, answer Copy (and on 3.7.8 Sync These Too), save changes When Quitting. On 3.5.0 and later, Export All Settings and Data to ~/corpus-fake/fake-export.itermexport.
Close Settings, Cmd-Q with one window open and confirm. The <ver> set is captured here.

Capture: tools/capture.sh copies, preserving paths relative to $HOME, the files listed in this manifest (it skips the iTermServer-<ver> executable and sockets) and lists other files changed since the last launch in changed-since-launch.txt.
3.4.0 has no multi-line paste warning in this flow because the paste went into a tmux window; no snippet tags; Snippets live in user defaults.
The first clean step did not remove a pre-existing ~/.config/iterm2 (a zsh glob error aborted that line), so it was removed from this set: it held only symlinks made by an earlier build.
